discovery: Twisted (magic-angle) graphene and moiré flat bands: prediction and discovery of correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, strongly correlated electrons, superconductivity)
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that rotating two graphene layers to a 'magic' angle of about 1.1 degrees would flatten the electronic bands and make the kinetic energy vanish. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group built such devices with a new tear-and-stack technique and found correlated insulating states and superconductivity that can be tuned simply with a gate voltage. This was a simple, bold experiment that turned a single material into a switchable platform for strongly correlated physics. It created the field of twistronics. Since then, laboratories around the world have reproduced and extended it, finding orbital magnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, fractional Chern insulators and superconductivity across many moiré systems. The twist angle is now a new design parameter for quantum matter, and these atomically thin systems let long-standing questions about unconventional superconductivity be tested directly.
